title: Endocrine System — DOMiNANCE Originals
source: KNUST Hormones lecture (Prof Fay): classification, signaling and steroidogenesis

questions.stem: What distinguishes endocrine secretion from exocrine secretion?

options.label: A
options.text: Release only into a glandular duct

options.label: B
options.text: Release only onto an epithelial surface

options.label: C
options.text: Release to blood or interstitial fluid

options.label: D
options.text: Release only inside a cell nucleus

options.label: E
options.text: Release directly into a synaptic cleft

questions.why: Endocrine tissues secrete chemical messengers into extracellular fluid for transport to target cells, unlike duct-mediated exocrine secretion.

questions.stem: Why does the same circulating hormone affect some organs more strongly than others?

options.label: B
options.text: All cells have identical hormone receptors

options.label: D
options.text: Hormones are active only near the gland

questions.why: Hormonal specificity primarily reflects the availability and nature of target-cell receptors.

questions.stem: Which combination governs the magnitude of a hormone-induced target-cell response?

options.label: A
options.text: Hormone level, organ size and blood group

options.label: B
options.text: Receptor number, pH and blood colour

options.label: C
options.text: Membrane size, urea level and temperature

options.label: D
options.text: Hormone level, receptor number and affinity

options.label: E
options.text: Cell shape, ATP level and capillary length

questions.why: The lecture identifies hormone concentration, receptor abundance and binding affinity as key determinants.

questions.stem: Why can thyroid hormones affect many tissues whereas ACTH targets relatively few tissues?

options.label: A
options.text: ACTH is secreted only into adrenal ducts

options.label: C
options.text: Thyroid hormone travels without blood flow

options.label: D
options.text: ACTH is immediately destroyed by all cells

options.label: E
options.text: Thyroid receptors occur only in thyroid tissue

questions.why: Most body cells express thyroid hormone receptors, whereas ACTH receptor expression is restricted to specific adrenal cortical cells.

questions.stem: Which tissue is recognized as an endocrine organ through its production of metabolic signaling substances?
questions.why: Adipose tissue secretes adipokines involved in energy balance and inflammation.

questions.stem: Which process is a principal integrated function of hormones?
questions.why: Hormones coordinate growth, reproduction, metabolism, stress responses and electrolyte balance.

questions.stem: Which hormone is classically classified as a glycoprotein rather than a simple peptide?
questions.why: FSH, LH and TSH are glycoprotein hormones.

questions.stem: Which hormone is an amino-acid-derived catecholamine?
questions.why: Epinephrine is a tyrosine-derived catecholamine, unlike cholesterol-derived steroids.

questions.stem: Which hormone is a cholesterol-derived steroid?
questions.why: Aldosterone is a steroid synthesized from cholesterol in the adrenal cortex.

questions.stem: Which class of chemical messenger generally requires cell-surface receptors because it does not diffuse readily through lipid membranes?
questions.why: Peptide hormones are hydrophilic and commonly signal through membrane receptors and intracellular transducers.

questions.stem: Which immediate target-cell response can be produced by some hormones without new protein synthesis?

options.label: B
options.text: Formation of a new endocrine gland

options.label: C
options.text: Opening or closing membrane ion channels

options.label: D
options.text: Synthesis of a complete cell nucleus

options.label: E
options.text: Replication of the entire cell genome

questions.why: Some hormone receptors rapidly alter membrane permeability or enzyme activity without waiting for transcription.

questions.stem: Which intracellular component converts ATP into cAMP after suitable G-protein signaling?
questions.why: Activated adenylyl cyclase generates cyclic AMP from ATP.

questions.stem: In a typical stimulatory G-protein pathway, what is the role of extracellular hormone?

options.label: C
options.text: It acts as the effector enzyme

options.label: D
options.text: It serves as the first messenger

options.label: E
options.text: It binds to newly synthesized DNA

questions.why: Hormone is the extracellular first messenger; cAMP is an intracellular second messenger.

questions.stem: Which signaling protein couples activated membrane receptors to adenylyl cyclase?
questions.why: G-protein α-subunits can regulate adenylyl cyclase following GTP binding.

questions.stem: What occurs to the guanine nucleotide on a stimulatory G-protein alpha subunit when its receptor activates it?
questions.why: Receptors promote GDP release and GTP binding; subsequent GTP hydrolysis helps terminate G-protein activity.

questions.stem: What is a principal immediate intracellular target of cAMP signaling?
questions.why: cAMP activates protein kinase A, which phosphorylates downstream substrates.

questions.stem: A hormone induces phosphorylation of intracellular regulatory enzymes via cAMP. Which sequence best explains it?
questions.why: G-protein stimulation of adenylyl cyclase increases cAMP, thereby activating PKA-dependent phosphorylation.

questions.stem: A receptor activates phospholipase C. Which membrane phospholipid is cleaved to produce IP3 and DAG?
questions.why: Phospholipase C cleaves PIP2 to yield diacylglycerol and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate.

questions.stem: Which intracellular effect follows binding of IP3 to its receptor?

options.label: A
options.text: Calcium synthesis from ATP in cytosol

options.label: C
options.text: Irreversible closure of every sodium channel

options.label: D
options.text: Conversion of DAG to free cholesterol

options.label: E
options.text: Direct transcription by IP3 in the nucleus

questions.why: IP3 opens calcium-release channels on the endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.stem: Which second messenger activates protein kinase C in the canonical PIP2 pathway?
questions.why: DAG remains associated with membranes and helps activate certain protein kinase C isoforms.

questions.stem: Which regulatory protein forms a calcium-dependent signaling complex with cytosolic calcium ions?
questions.why: Ca²⁺ binding to calmodulin alters the activity of downstream kinases and other target proteins.

questions.stem: A phospholipase C inhibitor prevents production of IP3 and DAG. Which early response would be impaired?
questions.why: Without IP3, hormone-induced calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum is reduced.

questions.stem: What is the common biosynthetic precursor of adrenal glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids?
questions.why: All steroid hormones derive from cholesterol through steroidogenic enzyme pathways.

questions.stem: Which product is generated by cleavage of the cholesterol side chain early in steroidogenesis?
questions.why: Conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone is the first key steroidogenic step.

questions.stem: Which adrenal cortical region lacks significant 17-alpha-hydroxylase activity and produces aldosterone?
questions.why: Zona glomerulosa lacks CYP17A1 activity and directs steroid production toward mineralocorticoids.

questions.stem: Which adrenal cortical zone primarily produces cortisol?
questions.why: Zona fasciculata synthesizes glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

questions.stem: What biochemical characteristic allows steroid hormones to cross the plasma membrane readily?
questions.why: Steroid hormones are small lipophilic molecules that can diffuse through membranes.

questions.stem: Which direct intracellular event commonly follows binding of a steroid hormone to its receptor?

options.label: B
options.text: Direct creation of cyclic AMP from ATP

options.label: C
options.text: Hydrolysis of membrane PIP2 by hormone

options.label: E
options.text: Immediate assembly of a spindle apparatus

questions.why: Steroid-receptor complexes regulate specific DNA-associated transcriptional programs.

questions.stem: Why do many steroid-hormone effects develop more slowly than ion-channel responses to peptide hormones?

options.label: A
options.text: They require synthesis of new cholesterol cells

options.label: B
options.text: They often require altered gene expression

options.label: D
options.text: They operate only through transducin GTPase

questions.why: Changes in mRNA and protein expression typically take longer than pre-existing enzyme or ion-channel modulation.

questions.stem: Which hypothalamic hormone initiates the central stimulation of cortisol release during stress?
questions.why: CRH stimulates pituitary corticotrophs to release ACTH, which then stimulates the adrenal cortex.

questions.stem: Which pituitary hormone directly stimulates adrenal cortical cortisol secretion?
questions.why: Anterior pituitary ACTH stimulates the zona fasciculata to increase cortisol production.

questions.stem: Rising plasma cortisol normally reduces both CRH and ACTH secretion through what mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Negative feedback at hypothalamus and pituitary

options.label: C
options.text: Direct calcium removal from target tissues

questions.why: The HPA axis is controlled by cortisol negative feedback on hypothalamic CRH and pituitary ACTH release.

questions.stem: Which organ is a major site of steroid-hormone inactivation and conjugation before excretion?
questions.why: The liver metabolizes many steroids and forms conjugates that facilitate elimination.

questions.stem: Which hormone principally supports renal sodium retention and potassium excretion?
questions.why: Aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid that promotes renal Na⁺ reabsorption and K⁺ secretion.
